chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:
The one in Ihram cannot get married. So if he were to do so, then his marriage would be invalid.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage for a person in the state of Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Safwan ibn Yahya, establishes the invalidity (batil) of marriage contracts for a muhrim, reflecting the juristic consensus that the state of Ihram imposes specific prohibitions on marital unions. Scholars note that this ruling underscores the spiritual focus required during Hajj, where worldly attachments like marriage are suspended to ensure undivided devotion to the pilgrimage rites.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Safwan, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘The one in Ihraam cannot get married. So if he were to do so, then his marriage would be invalid’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Safwan from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A person in the state of Ihram cannot marry, if one does so one’s marriage is invalid.’”
